appraisal_events.evidence: Elle demande tendrement: Quand est-ce que je vous revois ? — il ne répond que: quand je pourrai je vous ferai chercher, et le narrateur ajoute: Je n’osai lui dire que je voulais tout subordonner à la possibilité de voir Mme de Stermaria. Elle finit par concéder: Vous ne me recevrez que si vous le pouvez.
appraisal_events.explanation: In the aftermath of the physical encounter the narrator withholds any commitment and privately ranks Albertine below an absent woman, while free indirect style lightly ironizes her assumption that what they did must be the crowning of a great friendship. The asymmetry is the passage's dominant movement: she solicits and yields, he defers and conceals.

status_effects.explanation: She is left asking for a next meeting, has her sentimental construal of the encounter quietly undercut by the narration, and ends by granting him the right to refuse her at the door.
He gains local leverage: the timing of any further meeting is entirely his, and his real priority stays undisclosed, though the phrase Je n’osai qualifies the gain with a note of cowardice.
Absent from the scene, she is nonetheless elevated comparatively: the narrator would subordinate everything, including the woman he has just been intimate with, to the chance of seeing her.

ambiguities: The passage names Mme de Stermaria while the reference sheet lists only Mlle de Stermaria; read here as the same person under her married name, but a stricter era-name policy (as applied elsewhere on the sheet to prince des Laumes / duc de Guermantes) would treat the married form as a separate entry.

Albertine is present only pronominally in this window; the identification rests on the immediately preceding paragraphs, where she is named, and on the reference to ma tante. The window taken alone leaves the addressee underdetermined.
